Theme

Money, work & business

ownership noun

also right of ownership, possession, owning, proprietorship, title (to property)

classical

Liv. 45.13.15: dominium et jūs eōrum quī dederint esse (Lewis & Short)
Gai. Inst. 2.7 (Lewis & Short)

dominium, dominiī n.

noun, second declension

ownership, the right of an owner

The lawyers’ word for full ownership, as against possessiō, mere holding (Gai. Inst. 2.7). In speech Latin asks whose a thing is: cujus est?, and answers meum est (see own).

Other words

  • possessiō, possessiōnis f. — possession, holding; a property

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Mil. 75: hortōrum (Lewis & Short)

    Having and occupying a thing, whether or not one owns it in law; also the thing held, an estate (see property).

  • proprietās, proprietātis f. — ownership

    noun, third declension · also used · post-classical · Suet. Galb. 7: jūmentī (Lewis & Short)

    In Cicero a thing’s own nature, its peculiar quality; ownership only after Augustus (Suet., Dig.).

Examples

  • nūllīus bonī sine sociō jūcunda possessiō est

    no good thing is a pleasure to own without someone to share itSen. Ep. 6.4

See also own, master, property, property.
